5 Related Works Multi-Agent Cooperation and Competition. LLM-based multi-agent focuses on various agent profiles and interactions among agents (Wu et al. 2023;Guo et al. 2024;Li et al. 2023b). For instance, CoELA (Zhang et al. 2024c) investigated communication and cooperation in LLM-based watch-and-help tasks, while MindAgent (Gong et al. 2023) assessed the efficiency of collaboration between two or more agents. These efforts primarily focus on multiple agents collaborating effectively to achieve common goals (Panait and Luke 2005;Liu et al. 2023a). In contrast, some efforts focus on the competitive scenario between agents (Hu et al. 2024), like AgentPro (Zhang et al. 2024d) and ChessGPT (Feng et al. 2024) to evaluate the strategy reasoning and instruction following the ability of LLM-based agents in competitive settings. Suspicion-Agent (Guo et al. 2023) utilizes behavioral games theory (Akata et al. 2023) to evaluate the agent capabilities of LLM in a large set of two-player-two strategies games. However, most of these benchmarks evaluate only a few agents (Hu et al. 2024). Instead, our benchmark emphasizes the evaluation of multi-agent coordination and competition. Benchmarks using Games. A series of works investigated LLM-based game agents (Hu et al. 2024;Taesiri et al. 2024;Akoury, Yang, and Iyyer 2023;Hua et al. 2023). Several benchmarks center on the game Avalone e.g., Aval-oneBench (Light et al. 2023), CodeAct (Shi et al. 2023), and Recon (Wang et al. 2023a). Other benchmarks like CoS (Ma et al. 2023) and SwarmBrain (Shao et al. 2024), which excel in the strategy game StarCraft II (Vinyals et al. 2017). While MindAgent (Gong et al. 2023), ProAgent (Zhang et al. 2024d), and S-Agents (Chen et al. 2024), among others, focus on Overcooked (Carroll et al. 2019;Agashe, Fan, and Wang 2023) and Minecraft (BAAI 2023;Feng et al. 2023) in the context of agent collaboration (Wang et al. 2023b;Zhang et al. 2023;Li et al. 2023c). Moreover, in Minecraft, many efforts ask LLM to generate goals that adapt to the agent's current state, inventory, acquired skills, and environment (Li et al. 2023a). More benchmarks using games include Cradle (Tan et al. 2024), Thinker (Wu et al. 2024b), PokéLLMon (Hu, Huang, and Liu 2024), Pok-erGPT (Huang et al. 2024), CreativeAgent (Zhang et al. 2023), PlayDoom (de Wynter 2024), etc. LLMGA (Hu et al. 2024) further overviews the benchmarks into sixgame genres covering adventure, communication, cooperation, competition, simulation, exploration, and others. However, scarce work investigated multi-agent coordination and competitive scenarios. Even within this narrow field, their focus remains on two-agent interaction with unevenly distributed responsibilities.

Conclusion

This work introduces the BattleAgentBench, a benchmark for LLM-based multi-agent collaboration and competition evaluation, which defines seven sub-stages of three varying difficulty levels and conducts a fine-grained evaluation of language models in terms of single-agent scenario navigation capabilities, paired-agent task execution abilities, and multi-agent collaboration and competition capabilities. We perform a thorough evaluation of 11 LLMs. Although API-based models have demonstrated some collaborative capabilities, there is still enormous room for improvement.

Appendix 7.1 Evaluation Setup

We design 7 stages from easy to difficult for BattleAgentBench. Table 6 shows the detailed settings for each stage. The setting of the number of turns takes into account the cost factor of calling LLM. Increasing the number of turns may improve the scores of all models. However, the cost of calling the API will also increase accordingly. Therefore, we have set a relatively reasonable turn number for the unified evaluation of all models.

When evaluating each stage, we run multiple times and calculate the average score of the model to assess each model more accurately. For each run, we generate a random map by randomly sampling the agent's position within a small range. Specifically, for API-based models, we run each stage 3 times; for open-source models, we run each stage 5 times.
